newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan kerosene import increase seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Japan kerosene import increase seen continuing.

text.p: Japan's kerosene imports in July rose a sharp 109.9 percent from a year ago, and traders said they expected imports to continue to be higher each month compared to last year because of low kerosene stocks.

Japan's kerosene imports totalled 149,000 kilolitres (kl) in July, up 109.9 percent from a year ago and up 17.3 percent from June, according to the latest figures provided by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).
As a result, kerosene stocks at the end of July grew by 30.1 percent from the previous month to 3.04 million kl.
However, July's kerosene stocks remained 15.1 percent lower than levels posted in the same period a year ago. Kerosene stocks marked a year-on-year decline for the 15th consecutive month.
Oil product traders mainly attributed the high kerosene imports in July to Japanese refiners' low stocks, which need to be replenished ahead of the winter demand season.
Traders blamed reduced crude runs of between five and 10 percent which have been maintained since last year for low kerosene inventory.
They said they expect kerosene imports for the rest of the year to continue to be higher each month because of this low stock policy.
A trader with a Japanese oil refiner said that crude throughput is usually raised towards the end of the year, with the shift on production of kerosene.
Demand that cannot be covered by domestic production will be imported.
"I expect most oil product imports in the coming months to be either kerosene or jet fuel (and not other oil products)," he said.
He said demand for gas oil and gasoline in the coming months would probably be covered by domestic production, and large imports would probably not be needed.
Japan's gas oil production in July hit a record high of 4.2 million kl, up 8.1 percent from the same period a year earlier, MITI said.
The ministry attributed the rise in gas oil production to a substantial increase in the number of newly-registered cars using diesel.
MITI also said domestic sales of gasoline, gas oil and fuel oil A reached the highest levels ever for July.
Gasoline sales in July grew 2.6 percent from a year earlier to 4.8 million kl, and gasoline production also hit a high for the month at 4.57 million kl, up 10.9 percent from a year ago.
Gasoline stocks at the end of July totalled 1.87 million kl, down 5.8 percent year on year.
